questions.sec: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.unit: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.q: Endometrial hyperplasia (EH) is described in the overview as a ____ diagnosis.
questions.exp: Histopathology diagnosis is the first overview bullet; the cause, presentation and classification follow it.

questions.sec: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.unit: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.q: The cause given in the EH overview is ____.
questions.exp: Cause: up-estrogen (hyperestrogenic state) is printed under the heading.

questions.sec: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.unit: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.q: The typical EH presentation in the overview is a ____ woman with excessive bleeding.
questions.exp: Presentation: Perimenopausal female c/o excessive bleeding.

questions.sec: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.unit: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.q: EH is classified in the source under ____.
questions.exp: Classification: AUB - M, the malignancy/hyperplasia category of the PALM-COEIN system.

questions.sec: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.unit: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.q: Which is NOT one of the four EH overview bullets?
questions.exp: Tranexamic acid appears later as medical management of AUB, not in the overview list.

questions.sec: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.unit: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.q: After ruling out pregnancy, the first investigation listed for EH is ____.
questions.exp: 1st Ix (after r/o pregnancy): TVS up-ET -> suspect EH -> take EB.

questions.sec: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.unit: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.q: The investigation of choice (IOC) for endometrial pathology named here is ____.
questions.exp: IOC for endometrial pathology: Endometrial biopsy (EB).

questions.sec: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.unit: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.q: The gold standard listed in the EH overview is ____.
questions.exp: Gold standard: Fractional curettage + Hysteroscopy.

questions.sec: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.unit: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.q: In the investigations line, ET stands for ____ and TVS for ____.
questions.exp: The margin defines ET = endometrial thickness and TVS = trans-vaginal sonography.

questions.sec: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.unit: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.q: Match the EH investigation role: 1) First investigation 2) IOC 3) Gold standard with A) Fractional curettage plus hysteroscopy B) TVS C) Endometrial biopsy.
questions.exp: The overview assigns TVS, EB and FC+hysteroscopy to first, IOC and gold-standard roles.

questions.sec: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.unit: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.q: A perimenopausal woman has AUB and a thick endometrium on TVS; pregnancy is excluded. Which sequence follows the source overview?
opts: TVS first, then endometrial biopsy, with FC plus hysteroscopy as gold standard
questions.exp: TVS is the first test, EB the IOC, and FC+hysteroscopy the gold standard.

questions.sec: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.unit: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.q: I) The source calls TVS the first investigation after pregnancy is ruled out. II) It calls endometrial biopsy the gold standard.
questions.exp: TVS is first, but the gold standard is FC + hysteroscopy, not EB.

questions.sec: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.unit: Overview of EH, investigations and the AUB-M label
questions.q: A student reads 'Suspect EH, take EB' and concludes EB is the definitive gold-standard test. What is the source's actual hierarchy?
opts: EB is both IOC and gold standard
None of the three is preferred
EB is the IOC; the gold standard is FC + hysteroscopy
questions.exp: The arrows give TVS first, EB as IOC, and FC+hysteroscopy as gold standard; the roles are distinct.

questions.sec: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.unit: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.q: Endometrial sampling is also called ____ or endometrial aspiration cytology.
questions.exp: Endometrial biopsy/endometrial aspiration cytology head the sampling block at 00:04:35.

questions.sec: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.unit: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.q: Endometrial sampling is done in the ____ setting.
questions.exp: Done in: OPD; anaesthesia: Not required.

questions.sec: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.unit: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.q: The source states anaesthesia ____ for endometrial sampling.
questions.exp: Anaesthesia: Not required is the printed line.

questions.sec: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.unit: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.q: In India the named sampling instrument is ____.
questions.exp: Instrument used -> India: Karman's cannula; Pipelle and Vabra aspirator are the alternatives.

questions.sec: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.unit: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.q: Besides Karman's cannula, the sampling instruments listed are ____.
questions.exp: Pipelle and Vabra aspirator are the two other devices in the sampling list.

questions.sec: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.unit: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.q: Which is NOT a device in the endometrial-sampling list?
questions.exp: The ring applicator is a sterilisation instrument from the previous chapter.

questions.sec: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.unit: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.q: Match the age group to the endometrial-sampling trigger: 1) Reproductive age (<40 y) 2) Perimenopausal (FOGSI >=40 y / ACOG >=45 y) 3) Menopausal with A) EB irrespective of USG findings B) AUB plus risk factors or ET >=12 mm C) ET >=4 mm on TVS or AGCUS on Pap smear.
questions.exp: Each age column has its own printed indication set; do not swap their thresholds.

questions.sec: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.unit: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.q: In reproductive-age women (<40 y), sampling is indicated for AUB with risk factors of Ca endometrium such as ____.
questions.exp: C/o AUB + risk factors of Ca endometrium: PCOS, DM, HTN, Tamoxifen.

questions.sec: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.unit: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.q: The endometrial thickness threshold in the reproductive-age column is ET >= ____.
questions.exp: ET >= 12 mm is the reproductive-age trigger; 4 mm belongs to the menopausal column.

questions.sec: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.unit: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.q: AUB unresponsive to medical management with tranexamic acid, OCP or ____ is a reproductive-age sampling indication.
questions.exp: AUB unresponsive to medical mx (Tranexamic acid, OCP, progesterone).

questions.sec: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.unit: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.q: In the perimenopausal column the source recommends EB ____.
opts: only if the Pap smear is normal
questions.exp: EB irrespective of USG findings is the FOGSI/ACOG perimenopausal instruction.

questions.sec: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.unit: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.q: The perimenopausal age cut-off is >=40 years for FOGSI and >=____ for ACOG.
questions.exp: Perimenopausal (>=40 yrs: FOGSI / >=45 yrs: ACOG).

questions.sec: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.unit: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.q: In the menopausal column, the TVS trigger is ET >= ____.
questions.exp: Menopausal: ET >= 4 mm on TVS.

questions.sec: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.unit: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.q: The menopausal Pap-smear finding that triggers sampling is ____.
questions.exp: Pap smear: AGCUS (Atypical glandular cells of undetermined significance).

questions.sec: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.unit: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.q: I) The reproductive-age ET threshold is 12 mm. II) The menopausal ET threshold is 4 mm.
questions.exp: The two columns use 12 mm and 4 mm respectively; swapping them would misclassify patients.

questions.sec: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.unit: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.q: A 52-year-old postmenopausal woman has ET 6 mm on TVS. Which source indication applies?
opts: Menopausal ET >=4 mm on TVS triggers endometrial biopsy
No indication until ET reaches 12 mm
questions.exp: At 6 mm she exceeds the menopausal 4 mm threshold, so biopsy is indicated.

questions.sec: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.unit: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications
questions.q: Source-check: a 42-year-old with AUB and a normal USG is in the perimenopausal column. What does the source advise?
opts: Start tranexamic acid and never sample
Reassure because the scan is normal
Perform EB irrespective of the USG findings
Wait for ET to reach 12 mm
questions.exp: The perimenopausal instruction is EB regardless of ultrasound findings; thresholds are edition-specific study values.

questions.sec: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.unit: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.q: Hysteroscopy is annotated here as being used for ____ pathology.
questions.exp: Hysteroscopy: used for localised pathology, in contrast to fractional curettage.

questions.sec: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.unit: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.q: Fractional curettage (FC) is done in the ____.
questions.exp: Done in: OT; anaesthesia: GA (under general anaesthesia).

questions.sec: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.unit: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.q: The anaesthesia line for fractional curettage is ____.
questions.exp: Anaesthesia: GA (under general anaesthesia).

questions.sec: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.unit: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.q: The FC procedure begins with ____ curettage, then endometrial curettage.
questions.exp: Procedure: Endocervical curettage (1st) -> endometrial curettage.

questions.sec: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.unit: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.q: The stated advantage of FC is diagnosis of ____ endometrial pathology.
questions.exp: Advantage: Diagnosis generalised endometrial pathology.

questions.sec: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.unit: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.q: The stated disadvantage of FC is that it is ____ for localised pathology.
questions.exp: Disadvantage: Not good for localised pathology; hysteroscopy covers the focal lesions.

questions.sec: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.unit: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.q: The margin note names ____ as the single best investigation.
questions.exp: Note: Single best Ix -> Fractional curettage.

questions.sec: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.unit: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.q: Match the modality to its strength: 1) Hysteroscopy 2) Fractional curettage with A) Localised pathology B) Generalised endometrial pathology.
questions.exp: Hysteroscopy targets focal disease; FC samples the generalised endometrium.

questions.sec: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.unit: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.q: A focal endometrial polyp is suspected. Which source statement explains why FC alone may miss it?
opts: FC is the only test for focal lesions
FC is not good for localised pathology; hysteroscopy is used for focal lesions
TVS is the gold standard for polyps
questions.exp: FC samples generalised tissue and is poor for localised pathology; hysteroscopy is the focal tool.

questions.sec: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.unit: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.q: The 'EB Report Interpretation & Management' heading lists ____ EB outcomes.
questions.exp: EB outcomes: 1. Normal, 2. Metropathia hemorrhagica, 3. Endometrial hyperplasia +/- Atypia.

questions.sec: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.unit: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.q: Match each EB outcome to its next step: 1) Normal 2) Metropathia hemorrhagica 3) Endometrial hyperplasia +/- atypia with A) Progesterone (TOC) B) First-line AUB drugs, then FC+hysteroscopy if unresponsive C) Detailed hyperplasia management on the next sheet.
questions.exp: The flow chart routes normal, metropathia and hyperplasia to different next steps.

questions.sec: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.unit: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.q: For a NORMAL EB report, first-line AUB drugs are tranexamic acid, OCP and ____.
questions.exp: Use 1st line drugs to mx AUB: Tranexamic acid, OCP, Progesterone -> Oral / mirena.

questions.sec: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.unit: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.q: If a normal-EB patient is unresponsive to first-line drugs, the next step is ____.
questions.exp: Unresponsive -> FC + Hysteroscopy.

questions.sec: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.unit: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways
questions.q: Which is NOT a first-line drug in the normal-EB pathway?
questions.exp: Carboplatin is a chemotherapy drug from the endometrial-cancer chapter.

questions.sec: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.unit: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.q: Metropathia hemorrhagica is most common in a ____ female.
questions.exp: m/c: Perimenopausal female.

questions.sec: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.unit: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.q: The underlying pathology of metropathia hemorrhagica is ____ cycles.
questions.exp: Pathology: Anovulatory cycles.

questions.sec: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.unit: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.q: The bleeding pattern is amenorrhoea for 2-3 months followed by ____.
questions.exp: Amenorrhea x 2-3 months -> HMB (Heavy menstrual bleeding).

questions.sec: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.unit: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.q: The HPE of metropathia hemorrhagica shows a ____ pattern.
questions.exp: HPE: Swiss cheese pattern, proliferative endometrium, equivalent to cystic glandular hyperplasia.

questions.sec: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.unit: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.q: Metropathia hemorrhagica is described as equivalent to ____ hyperplasia.
questions.exp: Equivalent to cystic glandular hyperplasia.

questions.sec: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.unit: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.q: The risk of malignancy printed for metropathia hemorrhagica is ____.
questions.exp: Risk of malignancy: 1%; higher figures belong to EH with atypia.

questions.sec: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.unit: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.q: The treatment of choice (TOC) for metropathia hemorrhagica is ____.
questions.exp: mx: TOC: Progesterone -> Oral / mirena.

questions.sec: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.unit: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.q: I) Metropathia hemorrhagica follows anovulatory cycles. II) Its HPE shows a Swiss cheese pattern.
questions.exp: The pathology and HPE bullets are printed together.

questions.sec: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.unit: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.q: A perimenopausal woman has 2-3 months of amenorrhoea then heavy bleeding; biopsy shows a Swiss-cheese proliferative endometrium. Which source diagnosis and treatment fit?
opts: EH with atypia treated by TAH
Normal endometrium treated with tranexamic acid
questions.exp: The presentation, HPE and 1% risk define metropathia hemorrhagica; progesterone is the TOC.

questions.sec: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.unit: Metropathia hemorrhagica
questions.q: Which is NOT a metropathia hemorrhagica feature in the source?
questions.exp: Atypia is not listed; it belongs to the EH-with-atypia branch on the next sheet.

questions.sec: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.unit: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.q: Endometrial hyperplasia without atypia carries a malignancy risk of ____.
questions.exp: Risk of malignancy: 1-3% for EH without atypia; 8-30% with atypia.

questions.sec: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.unit: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.q: The next step after EH without atypia is ____.
questions.exp: Next step: Progesterone.

questions.sec: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.unit: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.q: Progesterone acts by downregulation of estrogen receptors, producing ____.
questions.exp: Downregulation of estrogen receptors -> Endometrial atrophy.

questions.sec: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.unit: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.q: The source prefers ____ over oral medroxy progesterone acetate for EH without atypia.
questions.exp: Mirena > Oral: medroxy progesterone acetate.

questions.sec: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.unit: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.q: For EH without atypia, ____ progesterone is preferred over cyclical.
questions.exp: Continuous > Cyclical is printed under the progesterone branch.

questions.sec: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.unit: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.q: Cyclical progesterone needs at least ____ days for a protective effect.
questions.exp: >= 12 days for a protective effect.

questions.sec: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.unit: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.q: The cyclical progesterone bullet notes ____ contraceptive benefit.
questions.exp: No contraceptive benefit is listed for cyclical progesterone.

questions.sec: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.unit: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.q: After treatment for EH without atypia, a repeat biopsy is done at ____.
questions.exp: Repeat biopsy at 3-6 months.

questions.sec: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.unit: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.q: If hyperplasia or bleeding persists at review, the next step is ____.
questions.exp: Hyperplasia (+)/bleeding (+) -> FC + Hysteroscopy.

questions.sec: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.unit: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.q: I) Continuous progesterone is preferred to cyclical. II) Cyclical progesterone has no contraceptive benefit.
questions.exp: The continuous-over-cyclical arrow and the no-contraceptive-benefit bullet are both on this sheet.

questions.sec: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.unit: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.q: A woman with EH without atypia is managed with oral cyclical progestogen. Which source caveat should be highlighted?
opts: A >=12-day course is needed for a protective effect and it gives no contraceptive benefit
questions.exp: The 12-day and no-contraception notes are edition-specific study points; Mirena and continuous therapy are preferred.

questions.sec: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.unit: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance
questions.q: Match the EH-without-atypia values: 1) Malignancy risk 2) Repeat biopsy 3) Minimum cyclical days with A) 12 days B) 1-3% C) 3-6 months.
questions.exp: Risk, surveillance interval and cyclical duration are three distinct printed numbers.

questions.sec: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.unit: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.q: Endometrial hyperplasia with atypia carries a malignancy risk of ____.
questions.exp: Risk of malignancy: 8-30% (up-up chance), far above the without-atypia figure.

questions.sec: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.unit: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.q: The next step for EH with atypia is ____.
questions.exp: Next step: FC + hysteroscopy.

questions.sec: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.unit: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.q: The best management for EH with atypia is ____.
opts: TAH (total abdominal hysterectomy, uterus plus cervix)
questions.exp: Best: TAH (Total abdominal hysterectomy -> Uterus + cervix).

questions.sec: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.unit: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.q: If a patient refuses TAH, the source offers ____.
questions.exp: Patient refuses TAH: Progesterone (megestrol).

questions.sec: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.unit: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.q: Failure or continued bleeding on megestrol leads to ____.
questions.exp: Failure/continued bleeding -> Hysterectomy.

questions.sec: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.unit: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.q: Match the EH branch to its risk and management: 1) Without atypia 2) With atypia with A) 8-30% risk, TAH best B) 1-3% risk, progesterone and repeat biopsy.
questions.exp: The two branches carry distinct malignancy risks and very different definitive management.

questions.sec: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.unit: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.q: Which is NOT an indication for FC plus hysteroscopy in the source note?
opts: Routine TVS screening at 3 weeks postpartum
questions.exp: Postpartum IUCD timing is a contraception topic, not an FC+hysteroscopy indication.

questions.sec: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.unit: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.q: An EB report of an ____ sample is one indication for FC plus hysteroscopy.
questions.exp: EB report: Insufficient sample is listed among the indications.

questions.sec: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.unit: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.q: ____ is another listed indication for FC plus hysteroscopy because it limits blind sampling.
questions.exp: In case of cervical stenosis appears in the indication list.

questions.sec: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.unit: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.q: EH without atypia plus ____ of medical management is the fourth indication.
questions.exp: EB: EH w/o atypia + Failure of medical mx.

questions.sec: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.unit: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.q: I) EH with atypia has a higher malignancy risk than EH without atypia. II) TAH is the best management for EH with atypia.
questions.exp: 8-30% exceeds 1-3%, and TAH is named the best treatment in the with-atypia branch.

questions.sec: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.unit: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.q: A biopsy shows EH with atypia; the patient declines hysterectomy and is started on megestrol, but bleeding continues. What does the source algorithm advise?
questions.exp: Failure/continued bleeding on progesterone is followed by hysterectomy.

questions.sec: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.unit: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy
questions.q: Source-check: a learner reads 'TAH -> uterus + cervix' and concludes removing the cervix is always optional. What is the source's definition?
opts: TAH removes the ovaries and tubes only
TAH here explicitly includes uterus plus cervix as the specimen
questions.exp: The printed expansion defines the operation; the surrounding atypia pathway treats it as definitive management, with the usual counselling caveats for any surgery.
